intro: The education system, grants and marks, and what happens in a student's head.
b1.texto:
**The stages.** **Educación primaria**, **secundaria** and **bachillerato**, then **la universidad** or **la formación profesional**. Schools are **públicos**, **privados** or **concertados** (private but state-funded), **laicos** or **religiosos**, sometimes **bilingües**.

**Subjects.** **Asignaturas obligatorias** and **optativas**. If you fail one, you have **una asignatura pendiente**. The phrase is also used in life: aprender a nadar es **mi asignatura pendiente**.

**Marks.** Out of ten: **suspenso** (below 5), **aprobado** (5–6), **notable** (7–8), **sobresaliente** (9–10). You **sacas un notable**; the teacher **pone las notas**. All your marks together are **el expediente**.

**Exams.** **Presentarse a** un examen, **examinarse de** matemáticas, **aprobar**, **suspender**, **repetir curso**, **pasar de curso**, **pedir una revisión**.

**Money.** **Solicitar** una beca, and the ministry **la concede** or **la deniega**. **La matrícula** is the enrolment fee.

**Degrees.** **Licenciarse en** Derecho, **hacer un máster**, **doctorarse**, **hacer la tesis**.

**Formats.** **Un curso presencial**, **a distancia**, **en línea**, **intensivo**; **la formación continua**.

**In your head.** **Memorizar**, **reflexionar**, **deducir**, **sacar conclusiones**, **quedarse en blanco**. The process is **el aprendizaje**.

**False friends.** **La carrera** is a university degree. **El colegio** is a school. **La facultad** is a university department, such as la Facultad de Medicina.
b2.f0: Carmela had got top marks in almost everything, and with that record she was counting on being granted the scholarship.
b2.f1: She had only one subject left to pass, which was moreover optional: History of Art.
b2.f2: She had sat the exam twice and both times her mind had gone blank in front of the examining board.
b2.f3: It was not lack of study: she had memorised everything, but she did not know how to draw her own conclusions.
b2.f4: A teacher advised her to stop repeating dates and learn to look at the paintings.
b2.f5: She spent the summer in museums, without notes, trying to work out for herself which period each work was from.
b2.f6: In September she passed with a good mark, and she says it was the only exam in which she really learnt something.
b4.pregunta: According to the text, why did Carmela fail the oral exam twice?
b4.o0.refuerzo: Se había quedado en blanco delante del tribunal.
b5.pregunta: According to the text, what did the teacher advise?
b5.o0.refuerzo: Que dejara de repetir fechas y aprendiera a mirar los cuadros.
b5.o2.refuerzo: The text does not say that.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Nine or ten out of ten.
b7.pregunta: Complete: I'm sitting the exam in June.
b7.o1.refuerzo: The verb needs a: presentarse a.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The verb needs a: presentarse a.
b8.pregunta: Estudió la carrera de Medicina means…
b8.o2.refuerzo: La carrera is the degree, not the working life.
b9.o0: She has been refused the grant.
b9.o1: They have given her the grant.
b9.o2: She has turned down the grant.
b9.o2.explicacion: The subject is they: they refused it to her.
b10.traduccion: My mind went blank in front of the teacher.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write an opinion essay on the education system of your country: what works and what should change.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Debate aloud: do exams really measure what a student knows?
